Still read by OilMarket.Floor for the three loot MEDALS that grant it (Speculator, Market Maker, Insider Trading); no perk may author it.

stats.Name: MarketVolatilityPct
stats.Description: Size of the market's per-tick swings. Pure gamble: wider swings mean better peaks to sell into and worse troughs to be caught in. Never touches the anchor, so it changes the risk and not the average payout.

stats.Name: MarketCrashPct
stats.Description: How far the CRASH ability drops the quoted oil price. 0 = the ability does not exist and the panel hides its button, so the first rank IS the unlock. Add, not PercentAdd: ranks read as "10/15/20% off", not as a multiplier of a multiplier.

stats.Name: MarketCrashSeconds
stats.Description: Seconds added to the crash window (base 45). The window is the whole difficulty of the ability - longer means more time to re-buy before the price recovers.

stats.Name: MarketCooldownPct
stats.Description: Crash cooldown, base 180 s. Meant to be bought NEGATIVE - a perk that shortens it - so -20% reads as what it does. Floored at 15 s.

stats.Name: ShotgunDamageFlat
stats.Description: FLAT damage added to every shotgun hit before the percentage perks multiply it (user call 2026-09-16). Per SHELL, split across the pellets - a flat on every pellet would pay a 12-pellet shell twelve times for one rank. So size ValuePerRank against a WHOLE SHELL, an order of magnitude above the pistol's rank - Item_Shotgun is 16 pellets x 60 damage, 960 a shell, and a pistol-sized rank would move it by well under one percent.

stats.Name: MeleeDamageFlat
stats.Description: FLAT damage added to every melee hit before the percentage perks multiply it (user call 2026-09-16). Per victim of a swing, like MeleeDamagePct. So one rank pays up to MeleeTargets times per swing (Item_Katana cuts 14), which is the opposite end of the family from the shotgun - size ValuePerRank well BELOW the pistol's.

stats.Name: FlameDamageFlat
stats.Description: FLAT damage added to every flame hit before the percentage perks multiply it (user call 2026-09-16). Spread over the burn, so one body set alight takes it once rather than once per burning second. The burn tick rounds to whole points four times a second, so this stat only moves in steps of roughly 4 x FlameBurnSeconds points (14 at the authored 3.5 s) and a rank under that does NOTHING - see the quantization note in HeldItem.Fire.
